issues.description: Console warning: 'Please ensure that the container has a non-static position, like relative, fixed, or absolute to ensure scroll offset is calculated correctly.' This appears twice, indicating a scroll-related component (likely a parallax or scroll observer) has a statically positioned container.
issues.root_cause: A component using a scroll offset library (e.g., react-scroll, framer-motion scroll, or a custom IntersectionObserver) has its parent container missing a non-static CSS position property. The container div in the landing page hero or scroll indicator section likely lacks position: relative.

issues.description: Background color may not be exactly #091829 (dark navy) as specified. The hero section background appears to be dominated by the room photo with a dark overlay, but the actual body/page background color behind the image is not verifiable as pure #091829 from the screenshot alone.
issues.root_cause: The global CSS or layout file may not explicitly set background-color: #091829 on the html/body or the main container, relying only on the hero image overlay.

fixes.reason: Adding 'relative' position to the hero section container resolves the console warning about non-static position for scroll offset calculation. The exact className string may vary; the key fix is ensuring position: relative is applied to the outermost scroll-tracked container.
Ensures the dark navy background color #091829 is explicitly set on the body, so it shows through before images load and in any gaps between sections.
